rationale: Headline is Theorem 3: HappyMap converges in O(1/alpha^2) iterations to a multicalibrated predictor; an algorithm-convergence bound fits existing class ALG.
Sample version (Thm 17) uses uniform-convergence concentration w.p. 1-delta; covariate-shift adaptation is an application, not a lift of the headline guarantee.
lifts=none, so code main modelling assumption: Lipschitz activations and input-independent 1-Lipschitz padding are explicitly stated; no separate evidence supplied.
No classes.csv code covers gauge-map output constraint of NN MPC policy; not RTA (no monitor), not CRL/NCERT/LUC; both coders chose NEW.
Guarantee is a w.p. 1-delta per-trajectory cost bound for a safe offline RL planner; certified RL fits better than generic generalisation bounds (GEN).
Eq. 20 bounds cost of each finite-horizon trajectory (length L) from current state; rule 6 picks smaller scope when tr vs op is doubtful.
Count-based concentration term (Lemma 4.2); bound holds only for in-distribution trajectories kept within data support by KL constraint (6) and condition (7).
Headline bound is analytical and never instantiated numerically; simulated and ad-platform results measure the planner (14.69% violations), not the guarantee.
Abstract states Pareto improvement 'can be guaranteed in theory'; Propositions 1-3 give conditional formal bounds over population D for DNN ensembles.
Inverse-variance/temperature-aligned ensemble guarantee matches no classes.csv code; C1's NEW label retained.
Evaluated only on MNIST/EMNIST, CIFAR, STL10, ImageNet/ObjectNet, ImageCLEF; no vehicle task.
Learned component is an image classifier (old/new DNN versions); codebook counts image classifiers as perception.
Propositions bound expected variance/MSE over the data distribution D, not a neighbourhood of one input.
Guarantee is an inequality on expectations (E_x Var, MSE) of the combined model.
No adversarial threat model; guarantee concerns natural sampling variation of D (tasks include dataset upgrade shift).
No Lipschitz, concentration, support or monitor argument carries the guarantee further; propositions stated directly at population level.
Main assumptions (aligned uncertainty, near-zero bias, MSE surrogate) are stated with citation [24] but not evidenced separately in the paper.
Headline reductions (48.1% via TS) come from benchmark datasets; codebook classes benchmark environments as simulated.
